Beseech

/bih-SEECH/ - rhymes with reach · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Beseech means to beg, plead, or implore.

The letter from the front does not ask so much as beseech: send word, send anything, tell me you are alive.

Worked Example

When the sentence was read, the defendant's mother rose from the second row to beseech the judge — hands pressed together, voice breaking — to let her son serve his term near home. The bailiff started forward; the judge waved him back and let her finish.

Beseech is the exact verb because it means to beg, plead, or implore — this is asking with the pride stripped out of it, urgent enough to interrupt a courtroom. Urge is a firm push and request is paperwork; beseech is what remains when neither has worked and everything is at stake.

How Beseech Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

implore

implore: the same desperate pitch, a shade more bookish

entreat

entreat: earnest asking, gentler and more old-fashioned

Antonyms

command

command: tells instead of asks, with power behind it

brush off

brush off: waves the plea away unheard

How Strong Is It? — urge → beseech → grovel

urge vs. beseech

urge vs. beseech: Urge is pressure with composure — a doctor urges a patient to rest and moves calmly on to the next chart.

grovel vs. beseech

grovel vs. beseech: Grovel goes further than beseech — the pleading collapses into self-abasement, forehead to the floor, dignity traded away entirely.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — be-

Prefix — be-: thoroughly, all about (Old English)

Root — seech

Root — seech: to seek (Middle English sechen, the old form of seek)

Put it together

Put it together: Be- (thoroughly) + seech (to seek) = to seek someone through and through. Middle English sechen is just seek in its older clothes; to beseech someone is to seek them out with your whole need showing. The pair survives in the old past form besought.

Use the root in a new word: seek

Use the root in a new word: seek: Rescue crews seek the lost hiker the way the root has always meant: to go after with purpose.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / dramatic

Beseech is begging in its Sunday clothes — save it for pleas where dignity has stepped aside: mercy, rescue, a life's favor. For daily asking, ask or urge; this unit's clamor is many voices demanding at volume, while beseech is one voice at someone's feet.
